title: Truncation triangles and cohomology of rational Weil pairs
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g_T=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ with geometric Frobenius, and $P_T=Lg_T^*$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use the rational/common-stage bounded constructible categories and Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:P_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$, whose arrows satisfy $u\theta_K=\theta_LP_T(u)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $W_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme and $W=W_0\times_{k_0}k$. For $m,i\in\mathbf Z$ use the standard bounded-constructible truncations and cohomology of [prop-constructible-truncations, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. With the canonical comparisons $c_K:P_W\tau K\simeq\tau P_WK$ characterized by compatibility with the truncation maps, for $\tau=\tau^{\le m}$ or $\tau^{\ge m}$ the rule
$$ (K,\theta_K)\longmapsto(\tau K,\tau(\theta_K)c_K),\qquad u\longmapsto\tau(u) $$
defines a functor on Weil pairs. Both canonical truncation maps and all three arrows of the standard truncation triangles are equivariant for the induced structures, including the shifted third arrow. Hence
$$ \mathcal H^i(K)=(\tau^{\ge i}\tau^{\le i}K)[i] $$
has the induced Weil structure and sends every Weil morphism to an equivariant map of cohomology sheaves. Forgetting these structures recovers the given truncations, triangles and cohomology functors; triangles here are in the underlying category.

For the ordinary or compact-support direct image to $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ whenever it is defined on the given bounded constructible objects and supplied with its canonical Weil lift, the induced maps on cohomology groups are Frobenius equivariant too. Precisely, write $A,B$ for two resulting point complexes, $u:A\to B$ for a Weil morphism, $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ for the point fiber functor and $\iota:\operatorname{Fib}_s\to\operatorname{Fib}_sP_s$ for the canonical point transport [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. Put $F_A=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\theta_A)\iota_A$ and similarly for $B$. Then
$$ \operatorname{Fib}_s(u)F_A=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\theta_B)\operatorname{Fib}_s(P_su)\iota_A=F_B\operatorname{Fib}_s(u), $$
and applying $H^i$ gives the asserted equation on ordinary or compactly supported cohomology. The statements hold at $E$ and in the common-stage category; no triangulated structure on the category of pairs is asserted.
